title: DSC 106 Portfolio
description: Build a personal course website with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, including responsive project cards, shared navigation, and a saved theme choice.

title: Food Processing Across Grocery Stores
description: Compare the share of foods predicted to be ultra-processed at Target, Walmart, and Whole Foods. Using the same food-category mix shows how much the stores' differences depend on the categories in the data.

title: Poverty Rates and Headcounts
description: Compare poverty rates and estimated numbers of people in poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa from 1990 to 2018. This ongoing group project explores how the choice of measure changes the argument about progress.

title: Campus Mobility Dashboard
description: Compare walking, cycling, and shuttle trips around a fictional campus. A map and travel-time filters could help students plan a route.

title: Reading Habits Explorer
description: Explore a fictional reading log by week and genre. Missing entries would stay separate from days with no reading.

title: Study Spaces
description: Compare fictional study spots by noise, seating, and opening hours. The idea is to help someone find a place that fits a quiet afternoon or a group session.

title: A Week of Campus Energy Use
description: Use a simulated building log to explore weekday and weekend energy use. Compare patterns while keeping units and measurement periods consistent.

title: Grocery Basket Comparisons
description: Compare the cost of the same fictional grocery basket across stores. Matching package sizes would help separate price differences from differences in quantity.

title: Walking Routes
description: Sketch several routes between fictional campus landmarks. Let readers compare distance, stairs, and shaded sections before choosing a walk.

title: Music Through the Week
description: Explore a made-up listening history by day and genre. A weekly view could show when listening happens without treating longer listening time as better.

title: Wait Times at Lunch
description: Use simulated observations to compare lunch queues. Show the range of waiting times alongside a typical wait so that variation stays visible.

title: Weekend Places to Explore
description: Arrange fictional parks, libraries, and museums on a simple map. Filters for travel time and cost could help someone plan a short trip.

title: Sleep and Study Logs
description: Display a fictional diary of sleep and study hours. Compare patterns across days while making clear that a pattern alone does not establish a cause.

title: Comparing Course Workloads
description: Compare made-up weekly time estimates for reading, practice, and projects. Keep the same scale across courses so readers can judge the differences directly.

title: Finding a Bike Rack
description: Map fictional bike racks and sample availability reports. Show when each report was recorded so an old observation is not mistaken for current availability.
